_comment: Scenario-specific behavior overrides for the Customer Support (contact centre) scenario. This is an OVERRIDE file only -- it supplements the generic config/ tree (categories, patterns, selection, protocol_codec, users, schema) rather than replacing it. Everything not specified here (canonical user/session schema, protocol & codec assignment, outcome determination, timestamps, packet counts, WAV references, validation, export) is still owned by the generic framework. Consumed by src/behavior_customer_support.py.

organization._note: All remaining internal users become Customer Support Agents; all external users become Customers. Actual counts scale with the run config's users target, so the roster grows/shrinks with the requested population size.

shifts._note: Shift sizing is weighted so on-shift agent coverage is heaviest across the researched 11:00-19:00 contact-centre peak window, with skeleton overnight coverage.

shift_sampling._comment: Used ONLY to decide which agents are plausibly on shift when pairing a call. The canonical start_timestamp is still produced by the generic engine's Stage 12 from the scenario's traffic_distribution -- this does not override it.

duration_model._source: Brown, Gans, Mandelbaum et al. (2005, JASA): a full year of real call-by-call bank contact-centre data showed service times are well-fit by a lognormal distribution -- not the exponential assumed by classic Erlang-C -- with type-dependent means of 115-401s.

ring_duration_model._source: Behan et al.: real provider average ring time ~10.0s, exponentially distributed. Note that 'no_answer' is NOT drawn from this model -- it is a genuine queue abandonment and uses the bimodal model below.

abandonment._comment: Applies to the 'no_answer' outcome: the caller waited in queue and hung up. Session span is bimodal, not a flat range.
abandonment._source: Brown et al. (2005, JASA): the empirical hazard rate of 'time willing to wait' at a real bank contact centre has two distinct peaks -- one within the first few seconds (callers who realise they are queued and hang up immediately), and a second around 60s, coinciding with the queue replaying its 'please wait' announcement.
